audit.why: Fizz favoured at 52.88% over 4559 games; Viktor has no dash, blink or escape in his kit text, so Fizz dictates every all-in. Difficulty 4/10 is consistent.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[5] and whys[6] are swapped: whys[5] sits on the 'First item' row but talks about the 2-item mark, and whys[6] sits on '2+ items' but talks about the first-item combo. Viktor's scaling engine is also called 'Hex Core', while Riot's text names it Glorious Evolution / Hex Fragments.
audit.why: Riot's passive text: Viktor gains Hex Fragments on kills, and every 100 permanently augments an ability. Nothing in the kit is called Hex Core. His R is 120/100/80s.
audit.corrected: First-item row describes the first-item one-shot; 2+ row describes late Arcane Storm zoning. Augments named as Hex Fragments / Glorious Evolution.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[0].text calls the shield 'Siphon Power (E)'. Siphon Power is Q; E is Hextech Ray. Content also calls his ultimate 'Chaos Storm' throughout, but the kit names it Arcane Storm. wants.you[0] cites 'E-Power Transfer', an ability that does not exist in this kit.
audit.why: Kit: Q Siphon Power (shield + auto reset, 9/8/7/6/5s), W Gravity Field (hardCC, 17/16/15/14/13s), E Hextech Ray (projectile line, 12/11/10/9/8s), R Arcane Storm (channel-interrupt zone, 120/100/80s). Fizz E Playful/Trickster is 16/14/12/10/8s and grants untargetability, which dodges the Arcane Storm tick and any timed burst.
audit.corrected: Real slot names and cooldowns used; the decisive interaction stated as Playful/Trickster's untargetable window versus Gravity Field's linger-stun and Arcane Storm's ticks.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns contains no number at all (lint COOLDOWN_NO_DIGIT).
audit.why: Gravity Field is the punishable cooldown at 17s rank 1, and Fizz's own E is 16s rank 1 — both belong in the field.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing on the page mentions that Viktor's combo opens with an auto-attack reset on Siphon Power, so the wind-up — not the cast — is the step-back cue.

edits.before: Q through him, W bleed, walk out through the wave — the fish phases in and out before his answer finds a target.
edits.after: Gravity Field stuns only if you linger — hop out with Playful/Trickster on cast, then commit while its 17s cooldown runs.

edits.before: Hopping in first against a held CC — the pole spent as an entrance is the whole kit spent as a coin flip.
edits.after: Even HP means his Q shield plus Gravity Field flips the dive — go on his W cooldown, not on boredom.

edits.before: Viktor whiffs Gravity Field and the lane briefly belongs to you.
edits.after: He walks home with no dash — Chum the Waters catches him in the open.

edits.before: - Viktor Gravity Field: matchup-defining — The stun zone owns every all-in — walk out the moment it drops or fight outside it. Check it before every step-up. - E Playful / Trickster is the lifeline; chip damage never gets it. - The ult answers fights, not waves.
edits.after: - Gravity Field (W): 17s at rank 1, 13s at rank 5 — the stun needs you to linger, so step out on the cast and fight the window after it. - Siphon Power (Q) is 9s early and is his only shield. - Playful/Trickster is 16s at rank 1; never spend it entering.

edits.before: Fish the strings and respect one spell — his CC is the lane; everything else is water.
edits.after: Fish the strings — his Siphon Power auto wind-up is the tell, Gravity Field the one spell.

edits.before: Viktor wins by landing Gravity Field, denying your pattern, and keeping the fight at a distance your kit resents.
edits.after: Viktor wins by stunning you in Gravity Field, shielding your string off with Siphon Power, and farming to his augments.

edits.before: Carry through deletions — shark, string, pole, repeat; one carry per fight is the contract and the pole notarizes it.
edits.after: Carry by removing Viktor himself — he has no dash, so a fog shark plus the full string ends him before Arcane Storm ever lands.

edits.before: Ahead, fish openly: zone Viktor with string threat, shark every river, and pole the counterplay — fed Fizz makes the map an aquarium.
edits.after: Ahead, deny the augments: Glorious Evolution needs kills, so take every crash to shark him off the wave and starve the upgrades.

edits.before: Viktor's Siphon Power (E) shield only helps him in extended trades, but he has zero mobility to escape once your E-slow lands, so you can punish him hard in short all-in windows before his passive Hex Core upgrades kick in.
edits.after: Viktor's shield sits on Siphon Power (Q), 9s at rank 1, and he has no dash to escape once Playful/Trickster's slow lands — punish in short all-in windows while that shield is down and before Hex Fragments augment his kit.

edits.before: Chaos Storm (R) is a delayed-follow zone control tool, not an escape, so Playful/Trickster lets you dodge it entirely and punish him while it's on cooldown.
edits.after: Arcane Storm (R) is a delayed zone tool, not an escape — Playful/Trickster goes untargetable through its ticks, and his 120s ultimate is then spent.

edits.before: Viktor becomes a genuine teamfight threat with Chaos Storm zoning and Hex Core augment scaling, so you need to shut down his farm early and force fights before he reaches his power spikes at 2-3 items.
edits.after: Viktor becomes a genuine teamfight threat with Arcane Storm zoning and Glorious Evolution augments bought by kills, so deny his farm and force fights on his 120/100/80s ult timer before he hits 2-3 items.

edits.before: Chaos Storm is a strong zone-control ultimate but it has a cast delay and doesn't let him escape, so Playful/Trickster lets you completely dodge the storm and then punish him while it's down for a long cooldown. He'll look to poke and control space with Gravity Field, but without kill pressure of his own he mostly just survives this phase rather than winning it. Keep applying pressure and look for picks whenever his cooldowns are down.
edits.after: Arcane Storm is a strong zone-control ultimate but it has a cast delay and doesn't let him escape, so Playful/Trickster's untargetable window rides out its ticks and leaves him a 120/100/80s cooldown to survive. He'll poke and control space with Gravity Field on 17s, but without kill pressure of his own he mostly survives this phase rather than winning it. Step up the moment that W is spent and look for picks.

edits.before: Viktor scales hard into a teamfight-controlling mage once he has Hex Core augment upgrades and a couple of items, with Chaos Storm capable of zoning entire fights and Gravity Field locking down flanks. If you've built a lead in lane, keep pressuring side lanes and picking him off before teamfights happen rather than letting him set up from a safe backline position. Denying his early farm is the single biggest lever you have to keep him from reaching his late-game ceiling.
edits.after: Viktor scales into a teamfight-controlling mage once Hex Fragments augment his abilities and a couple of items land, with Arcane Storm zoning entire fights and Gravity Field locking down flanks. His augments are bought with kills, so every takedown you deny slows the whole engine. Keep pressuring side lanes and picking him off before teamfights start rather than letting him set up from a safe backline seat.

edits.before: Punish his lack of mobility with all-in trades whenever E-Power Transfer is down
edits.after: Punish his lack of any dash with all-in trades whenever Siphon Power (Q) is down

edits.before: Land Chaos Storm to zone teamfights once Hex Core is upgraded
edits.after: Land Arcane Storm to zone teamfights once his augments are online

edits.before: Level 6 Chaos Storm is a zone tool, not an escape, so your ult lets you dodge and punish it cleanly
edits.after: Level 6 Arcane Storm is a zone tool, not an escape, so Playful/Trickster dodges its ticks and you punish

edits.before: The 2-item mark still favours you since Viktor needs Hex Core upgrades before his kit truly threatens you
edits.after: First item favours you: the shark-string one-shots him before Hex Fragment augments make his kit threatening

edits.before: Your first-item burst combo kills him before his own damage output catches up, keeping this phase in your favour
edits.after: At two-plus items you still erase him first, though his Arcane Storm zoning starts to decide fights you are not in
